solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Duly pick out fair game?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the two words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to choose a quarry duly, as though it were legitimately fair game for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' looks like the hunter's idiom, but it is a game at a fair; 'out' rearranges DULYPICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip is a fairground or fete attraction where you pay to pull a random prize from a tub, so it is a game at a fair.

clue.text: Page item, tiny piece

parts.note: an item in a newspaper is an article

explanation.surface: A list describing a page item as just a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and everyday speech a particle is a minute fragment of matter, a speck.

clue.text: Academic ignoring American in workroom

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave out part of the word that comes before it

parts.note: an academic, bookish person is studious

explanation.surface: A scholar pays no attention to an American colleague in the workroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academic' looks like a noun for a person, but here it is the adjective, giving STUDIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist, photographer or craftsperson works.

clue.text: Customer apt to dither? Right on!

indicators.note: to dither is to waver nervously, so the three letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a customer is likely to hesitate, then answers with an approving 'Right on!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt' reads as 'likely', but it is the anagram fodder for PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop, restaurant or other business.

clue.text: Country record includes live song

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the next one inside it

parts.note: to bug a room is to record conversations secretly with a hidden microphone
L is the abbreviation for live, as on electrical wiring
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A national record contains a song performed live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a disc, but it is the verb, as a spy would record: BUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a nation in south-eastern Europe on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Clubs, later, reformed syndicate

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Golf or social clubs later reorganised into a business syndicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an association of businesses combining to control prices, a syndicate.

clue.text: Status seeker on horseback, in front of jump

indicators.note: in front of places the riding piece before the jumping piece in the answer

parts.note: a jockey who is up is mounted, riding a horse
to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: An ambitious rider gets ahead of a jump at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in rank who behaves arrogantly, a social climber.

clue.text: Excellent management, but lacking foresight

indicators.note: lacking means part of the longer word is missing

parts.note: supervision is management or oversight of work
vision is foresight, the ability to plan ahead

explanation.surface: Management may be fine but shows no foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Eccentric back with university, the French count

indicators.note: back means the word for an oddball is written in reverse

parts.note: a card is an old word for an eccentric or amusing person
la is the French feminine for the

explanation.surface: An odd Frenchman returns to the university with a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' seems an adjective; it is the noun CARD, an amusing oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the vampire nobleman of Bram Stoker's novel, styled Count Dracula.

clue.text: Wealthy old lady's flutter after function

indicators.note: after places the bet piece behind the party piece in the answer

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
a flutter is a small bet, a wager

explanation.surface: A rich elderly lady has a little bet after a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' looks like nervous excitement; in Britain a flutter is a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding property or title from her late husband, typically an elderly lady of means.

clue.text: Ram a truck's rear wheels and this may be broken

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns around, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Ramming a lorry's back wheels may well wreck them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' looks like the truck's tyres, but it turns TUP + A + K backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is informal for broken or no longer working, from German.

clue.text: Completely at a disadvantage, the Conservatives

parts.note: being down is losing or behind, at a disadvantage
the political right is the conservative wing

explanation.surface: The Conservative party is entirely on the back foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means utterly or thoroughly.

clue.text: Chief administrator, noted career girl in resort

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notable career woman runs things at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is a holiday place in the surface but means re-sort here.
explanation.definitionFit: A director-general is the head of a large organisation such as the BBC.

clue.text: Saw rambler in pub, disheartened

indicators.note: in means the walker sits inside the remaining outer letters
disheartened means losing its heart, the middle letter

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer or rambler

explanation.surface: A hiker is seen in a pub, looking downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying, a maxim.

clue.text: Go beyond social welfare?

definitions.meaning: community work taking help to people where they live

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to exceed; as a noun it is a programme of social help brought to people.

clue.text: Beset with bees bumbling around one, say

indicators.note: around means the jumbled insects go round the other pieces
bumbling means moving clumsily, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by bees buzzing around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beset' and 'bees' share letters, tempting a straight anagram; 'say' is the usual crossword signal for EG, an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset and to besiege both mean to surround and harass.

clue.text: Resume painting after nap

indicators.note: after places the painting piece behind the nap piece

parts.note: a nap is a rest
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: An artist goes back to work on a picture after a snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin again after a break, to resume.

clue.text: Cook, perhaps, posed with flag on roof of theatre

parts.note: an artist's model sat, or posed
the flag is a name for the iris flower

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof of a word is its top, first letter

explanation.surface: A chef posed with a flag on top of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook is Peter Cook, the British comedian of the 1960s satire boom, not a chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Cook was a leading British satirist, an example of one who mocks through humour.

clue.text: Number Ten upset about empty emporium, large building in Scotland?

indicators.note: about means the number pieces go on either side of the emptied word

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: upset means the three letters are tipped into a new order
empty means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Downing Street is unsettled by an empty shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TEN into ENT; 'about' sets TEN and ENT on either side of EM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a tenement is a large building divided into flats.

clue.text: Hurry to one at Skegness, rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged means all fifteen letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A rushed trip to someone in Skegness, a seaside town on the English east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Get one's skates on is a British idiom meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Light out around Cape causes a sudden problem

indicators.note: around means the shaken letters go round the next piece
out means the letters are out of their usual order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A lamp failing near a headland causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LIGHT to GLITH, and 'around' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden malfunction or hitch, especially in a machine.

clue.text: Name weapon limited in scope

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A weapon is said to have a restricted range.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means restricted, of small extent or range.

clue.text: Tackle school producing tasteless art

parts.note: tackle is equipment, kit

explanation.surface: Equipment from a school produces vulgar artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art regarded as garish, sentimental and in poor taste.

clue.text: Reprimand son towards the end

parts.note: late means near the end of a period

explanation.surface: A son is told off near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is British informal for to criticise severely or scold.

clue.text: Fashionable boy's name, reportedly? Seriously

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: Ernest is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks, without joking, whether a boy's name is trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: In earnest is an idiom meaning sincerely, not joking.

clue.text: True male domain

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A genuinely male territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or field of activity, a domain.

clue.text: Ride a bike, holding on in tropical storm

indicators.note: holding means the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bike

explanation.surface: A cyclist battles on through a tropical storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a violent rotating tropical storm.

clue.text: Channel Islands firm demonstrating a tank

parts.note: stern means firm or strict

explanation.surface: A firm from the Channel Islands, British islands off France, shows off a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a water tank, as in a loft or above a toilet.
